scope.problem: Couples without design skills need to create and share a polished mobile wedding invitation page (date, venue, RSVP, gallery) quickly and affordably.
scope.audience: Engaged couples in their 20s-30s planning a wedding, primarily on mobile, in Korea and similar markets.
jobs: Create an invitation from a template and personalize text, photos, and theme
Share the invitation link via messaging apps
Collect RSVP responses and congratulatory messages
Show venue location, directions, and account transfer info for gifts
featureScope: feat.templates: Template gallery - pre-designed invitation templates the user can pick and customize (p0)
feat.rsvp: RSVP collection - guests submit attendance, headcount, and meal preference (p0)
feat.gallery: Photo gallery - couple photo gallery with lightbox viewing (p1)
feat.map: Venue map and directions - embedded map, transit guidance, and parking info (p0)
feat.gift: Gift account info - bank account reveal for congratulatory money, per side of the family (p1)

brandConstraints.notes: Client-specified values override design-system default colors/fonts downstream; unspecified properties use the selected system's defaults.

competitors.name: Barunson Mcard (바른손카드 모바일청첩장)

rationale.sharedProblem: Lets couples without design skills produce a polished mobile wedding invitation page quickly; marketed as free/unlimited mobile invitation creation, directly addressing the affordability angle of the PRD problem.
rationale.sharedAudience: Korean engaged couples in their 20s-30s preparing weddings on mobile; Barunson is Korea's best-known wedding invitation brand and its Mcard product targets exactly this segment.
sharedJobs: Create an invitation from a template and personalize text, photos, and theme
Share the invitation link via messaging apps (link copy and QR code from My Page)
Show venue location, directions, and account transfer info for gifts (약도/map image, 축의금 계좌번호 reveal)
featureOverlap: feat.templates - large mobile invitation template gallery (Product/MobileInvitationList, Product/Detail pages)
feat.gallery - couple photo gallery within the invitation page
feat.map - venue map/directions section (약도 image, QR usage)
feat.rsvp - attendance-check function on invitation pages

accessLimitations: Building or previewing a personalized invitation requires Barunson account signup/login; My Page features are not publicly crawlable
Some feature explanations live in FAQ pages split across desktop (www.barunsoncard.com) and mobile (m.barunsoncard.com) domains, and parts are rendered as images rather than quotable text
Template detail pages show sample invitations; live customer invitations are private links

competitors.name: 데어무드 (Theirmood)

rationale.sharedProblem: Couples without design skills need a polished, shareable mobile wedding invitation page quickly and affordably; Theirmood sells exactly this as a flat-priced Korean SaaS (~19,800 KRW) with free draft creation and unlimited editing until the wedding date.
rationale.sharedAudience: Engaged Korean couples in their 20s-30s planning weddings on mobile, sharing invitations via KakaoTalk — the same primary audience and market as the PRD.
sharedJobs: Create a designed mobile invitation page from templates without design skills
Show wedding date, venue map, and directions automatically from the venue address
Collect RSVPs with attendance tracking, KakaoTalk notifications, and Excel export
Display a photo gallery (up to 100 photos, multiple layouts)
Share the invitation link with guests via mobile messaging
featureOverlap: RSVP system with automated attendance tracking
Auto-generated venue map, directions, and transport info
Guestbook and guest photo upload (QR-based 'snap') features
Flat affordable one-time pricing, free draft before purchase

accessLimitations: Editing dashboard and management features require sign-up/purchase; homepage marketing content was verified, not the logged-in editor
Some review counts on the homepage render obscured (e.g. '00+') without JS

competitors.name: 연서 (Yeonseo)

rationale.sharedProblem: Couples want a polished mobile invitation without hiring a designer; Yeonseo advertises creating and sharing a complete mobile invitation in about 5 minutes for a single low one-time price (₩9,800 for one year).
rationale.sharedAudience: Korean engaged couples in their 20s-30s, mobile-first, sharing invitations through KakaoTalk — matching the PRD's audience and market.
sharedJobs: Build a template-based mobile invitation page quickly with no design skills
Present date, venue, and directions (Kakao/Naver/Tmap map integration)
Collect RSVPs and congratulatory guestbook messages from guests
Show a wedding photo gallery (up to 30 photos, slideshow or grid)
Share via KakaoTalk card, short URL, and QR code
featureOverlap: Venue map and transit guidance integrations
Bank account info display with one-click copy

accessLimitations: Invitation editor and RSVP management require account sign-up; only public marketing pages were verified
Site content is Korean-only

competitorRanking.rationale: Yeonseo has the strongest evidence coverage: every card is observed, and the public /sample live invitation directly shows the guest-facing RSVP form, gallery, directions, and per-side account rows with copy buttons — actual rendered UI rather than marketing claims. Its curated four-style template families and letter-styled visual direction (serif type, ivory/deep-green palette) make it the most concrete design reference, even though the observed RSVP form omits the PRD's headcount/meal fields and parking info was absent.

Theirmood matches the PRD feature-for-feature most completely: its RSVP covers all three PRD fields (attendance, companion headcount, meal) plus a dashboard and Kakao notifications, its map deep-links to Kakao/Naver/Tmap with parking info, and its gift section adds one-click copy and KakaoTalk transfer. The weakness is evidence quality — nearly all cards rest on homepage marketing feature lists (medium reliability) rather than an operated invitation, and the template-count card is currently unknown after a failed re-fetch.

Barunson Mcard covers all PRD areas and has a genuinely differentiated gift flow (card-paid 축의금 converted to points with per-side settlement, documented in first-party FAQ), plus a large ~100-template gallery with public previews. But its RSVP and directions evidence is only indirect (Area_Name identifiers in template JSON, with map support possibly a static uploaded 약도), and live invitations are private, so it offers the least observable guest-facing UI to distill design references from.

references.title: Kakao Developers — Kakao Talk Share & Message Template docs
references.whyRelevant: Official spec for the 'share invitation link via KakaoTalk' task: defines the share flow and the message-template structure (image + text + up to 2 buttons) the invitation share card must fit.

references.title: Kakao Maps JavaScript Web API (apis.map.kakao.com)
references.whyRelevant: Official docs for the embedded venue-location map: free quota, markers for the venue pin, and HTML custom overlays usable for a styled venue label/directions bubble.

references.title: Bliss & Bone — Wedding Website RSVP: Setup, Etiquette & Tracking Guide
references.whyRelevant: Domain-specific RSVP UX conventions: which questions to ask (attendance, guest count, meal), form length targets, deadlines, and host-side response tracking — maps directly to the RSVP collection task.

references.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Website Forms Usability
references.whyRelevant: General form-usability heuristics (single column, minimal fields, label placement) that apply to the mobile RSVP form and the invitation text-personalization editor.

references.title: Collect UI — Daily User Interface Inspiration
references.whyRelevant: Free-to-browse UI shot gallery (categories browsable without login) usable for visual references for card/gallery layouts, event pages, and form styling; a free substitute for the off-limits paid libraries.

references.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Carousels on Mobile Devices
references.whyRelevant: Research-based guidance for the swipe photo-gallery pattern that all three top competitors advertise (Yeonseo slide layout, Theirmood swipe/thumbnail-swipe, Barunson 30-photo gallery): swipe support, weak dot signifiers, and reachability of items in few steps.

references.title: MDN — Web Share API
references.whyRelevant: Official spec for the OS-level share fallback behind KakaoTalk sharing: confirms sharing must be user-initiated (transient activation / button tap), matching the Kakao Share model of an explicit in-page share button and covering non-Kakao messengers.

referenceDistillation.direction: Optimize the three guest tasks for one-tap completion. RSVP: a form finishable in under two minutes covering attendance, companion headcount, and meal preference (Theirmood's field set fills the gap in Yeonseo's observed minimal form), with a visible deadline and host-side response tracking. Gifts and directions: per-account one-click copy plus KakaoTalk transfer linking, and deep links out to Kakao/Naver/Tmap navigation apps with transit and parking details. Sharing and gallery: explicit user-tapped share buttons (Kakao Share feed template with one hero image and at most two short buttons, Web Share API as the OS-level fallback) and a swipe-first photo gallery that does not rely on dot indicators alone.
referenceDistillation.rationale: Task patterns come mainly from rank-2 Theirmood, which the ranking calls the most complete PRD match: its RSVP card covers all three PRD fields plus dashboard and Kakao notifications, its directions card names Kakao/Naver/Tmap deep links with parking info, and its gift card documents one-click copy plus 카톡 송금 — while rank-1 Yeonseo's observed sample proves the per-relative copy-button row pattern in rendered UI but omits headcount/meal, so the two are combined. Platform docs (Kakao Share's manual-selection model, Web Share's user-gesture requirement) and the Bliss & Bone two-minute/deadline guidance anchor the completion-budget and share-button decisions independently of competitor marketing.

referenceDistillation.direction: Structure the invitation as a single scrolling mobile page with a fixed section order — hero photo, greeting, photo gallery, 오시는 길 (venue and directions), 마음 전하실 곳 (per-side accounts), RSVP — where each section is an independently toggleable module the couple can switch on or off. Group congratulatory-money accounts under 신랑측/신부측 headers with one row per relative (bank, holder, number, copy button), following Yeonseo's observed sample. Keep the RSVP form single-column with minimal fields per NN/g form guidance, and let template selection happen through full live-sample previews rather than static thumbnails.
referenceDistillation.rationale: The section inventory is corroborated across all three ranked competitors: Barunson's public preview JSON names 갤러리, 오시는길, RSVP, and 축의금송금 areas and its FAQ documents ON/OFF section toggles; Yeonseo's live /sample invitation actually renders the gallery, directions, per-side account rows, and RSVP form in that scrolling order — the only guest-facing page observed end-to-end, per the rank-1 rationale. Theirmood's 100-photo multi-layout gallery card justifies treating the gallery as a configurable module rather than a fixed strip.

referenceDistillation.direction: Adopt Yeonseo's letter-styled classic direction as the primary visual reference: serif Korean typography, an ivory ground with a deep-green accent, and a small set of curated, named style families (클래식/모던/미니멀/빈티지) rather than Barunson's commerce-style grid of ~100 skins. Lead every theme with the couple's photo as the hero, echoing Barunson's photo-card mockup presentation, and carry the theme's typography and colors into embedded widgets — e.g. an HTML custom overlay on the venue map — so no section breaks the invitation's mood. Use Collect UI shots only as a taste board for soft-palette card layouts, not as interaction evidence.
referenceDistillation.rationale: The rank-1 competitor's strongest observed asset is its visual identity: the live homepage capture shows serif type, ivory/deep-green palette, and a letter metaphor, and its template model is four curated families previewable as complete live samples (recognition over recall). Barunson (rank 3) evidences the opposite pole — a large image-heavy skin marketplace — which the ranking rationale treats as less distillable; the curated direction is therefore the better-grounded style reference. The Kakao Maps custom-overlay card supplies the mechanism for extending that theme into the map section.

ideas: Offer a live per-template sample preview (Barunson embeds a /preview/{id} iframe on each template detail page) so users can judge designs before signing up — recognition rather than recall.
Prefill editor fields from the chosen template and defer optional sections, per NN/g guidance to remove fields that can be derived, deferred, or omitted.
Differentiate on curation quality over raw count: Barunson markets '100여종의 스킨' via image-heavy pages; a smaller, well-tagged gallery with fast lightweight previews could feel better on mobile.
Keep the guest form under a two-minute budget: attendance yes/no, headcount, meal preference only, single-column with labels above fields (Bliss & Bone + NN/g).
Barunson's RSVP scope (headcount/meal collection) is unverified publicly — shipping the PRD's full headcount+meal form with a host response dashboard is a credible differentiation candidate.
Surface the RSVP deadline prominently on the form and give hosts a response-count dashboard (three-to-four-weeks-before convention).
Match Barunson's baseline: ~30-photo capacity with the gallery as an ON/OFF toggleable section of the invitation.
Lightbox full-screen viewing (the PRD's interaction) was not confirmed at Barunson — a polished swipeable lightbox is a low-cost differentiation candidate.
Use Collect UI as a taste board for hero-photo-led, soft-palette gallery layouts (aesthetic direction only, not interaction evidence).

Embed an interactive Kakao Map with a venue marker plus copy-address and open-in-Kakao-Navi actions; Barunson's template hints at a static 약도-image fallback in some contexts, so a true interactive map can exceed the observed baseline.
Use a Kakao Maps HTML custom overlay for the venue name/hall bubble so the map keeps the invitation's typography and colors.
Include explicit transit-guidance and parking-info text fields — neither was confirmed in Barunson's public template structure.
Ship the PRD baseline as collapsible per-side (신랑측/신부측) account reveals with one-tap account-number copy — the simple flow Barunson wraps inside a heavier points system.
Barunson goes beyond static display with card-payment 축의금 that settles per side; treat in-page payment as a later roadmap item, not MVP.
Adopt Barunson's error-prevention lesson: route and label everything strictly by family side to avoid misdirected transfers.

cards.claim: Mobile photo carousels must support swipe as the primary navigation gesture, dots alone are weak signifiers users often miss, and users should reach the last item within a few taps or swipes — directly applicable to the invitation's couple photo gallery (competitors advertise slide/swipe layouts of up to 30-100 photos).

source.context: Article 'Carousels on Mobile Devices', recommendations on carousel navigation and signifiers

proof.quote: Make sure your carousel supports swipe.

limitations: General mobile-carousel research, not wedding-invitation specific; the article also cautions against burying important content deep in a carousel, which argues for pairing the swipe gallery with a grid/mosaic view for large photo sets.
The 3-4 step reachability guidance applies to content-critical carousels; a browsing-oriented wedding gallery can tolerate more items.

uxHeuristics.task: Guest browses the couple's photo gallery
uxHeuristics.note: Support swipe on the gallery and do not rely on dots alone as position indicators; offer a grid layout for large sets so photos beyond the first few remain discoverable.

decisionRationales: All Barunson evidence is first-party (homepage marketing, FAQ, template JSON); guest-facing flows sit behind login or private invitation links, so interaction details (lightbox behavior, RSVP field scope, map interactivity) need a hands-on account audit before being treated as confirmed.

Barunson's RSVP is only structurally evidenced ('Area_Name':'RSVP') with headcount/meal collection unverified, so a short, reference-guided RSVP form (two-minute budget, single column, deadline + host dashboard) is the clearest differentiation opportunity in the PRD scope.

An interactive Kakao Maps embed (marker + themed HTML overlay, free tier with daily quota) is technically low-risk and may exceed Barunson's observed baseline, whose template hints at a static uploaded 약도 fallback in some contexts.

Consistency audit outcome: all 16 cards already satisfied the status taxonomy (observed cards carry verbatim quotes; unreachable-site cards were correctly marked 'unknown' rather than absence), and no contradictions or duplicate claims were found — no downgrades or merges were applied.

Per reviewer decision (qa-round-1), the defunct DDD Project (domain listed for sale, all evidence unknown) was replaced with two live competitors: Theirmood and Yeonseo. Its dead-domain investigation details live in the round-1 revision history (package.v1.json).

Stage restructure applied per team feedback + qa-round-2: references were re-derived from the autonomous top-3 competitor ranking into three categories (style/layout/interaction); stage-3 human confirmation removed, internal live verification retained.

The wrong-path guess /CustomerService/FAQ also returned no FAQ content (real FAQ lives at /Customer/Faq).

The invitation builder, My Page order management, and guest-facing RSVP/gift/map interactions require Barunson account login or a private customer invitation URL; RSVP field details (headcount, meal preference), lightbox behavior, and map embed type could not be observed publicly. The public /preview/{id} sample pages render their sections client-side via JavaScript, leaving only structural JSON observable.

dribbble.com/tags/wedding-invitation rendered as an empty page via the fetcher (JavaScript-only content), so no verbatim quotes could be captured; Dribbble was dropped even though browsing appears free in a normal browser.

dalpeng.com homepage was reachable but rendered mostly as a marketing shell with image placeholders and no pricing/RSVP/gallery product content, so it was rejected as insufficient evidence of a live matching product.

bojagicard.com is live but is primarily a printed paper invitation shop (50-unit minimum orders) with mobile invitations only as a secondary category, so it does not match the PRD's core problem and was dropped.

The invitation editor, RSVP dashboard, and management features sit behind sign-up/login (theirmood.com/login); only homepage marketing copy could be verified, so no card is based on operated product UI.
Some homepage counters (e.g. review counts rendered as '00+') are populated by JavaScript and were obscured in the fetched static HTML, so social-proof numbers could not be captured.

The invitation editor and host-side RSVP/guestbook management dashboard require account sign-up (/login); only public marketing, help, and sample pages were examined, so editor customization depth, RSVP field configuration (headcount/meal options), and management views could not be verified.

No public page confirmed lightbox photo viewing, parking-info fields, or rendered Kakao/Tmap map buttons; the sample invitation showed only a Naver Map link and contained no 주차 (parking) text. These remain unverified rather than absent.
